contexts: 520-bed teaching hospital, adult medical and surgical wards
vascular access flowsheet in the electronic health record
reading: The policy acts through dwell time: catheters stay longer, fewer are inserted, and shift-by-shift site assessment carries the safety load. The retrieved records show little change in failure and no rise in phlebitis with longer dwell where sites are scored, but infiltration rises after the fourth day in older patients and documentation weakens at night and at weekends. Patients who need many catheters are sicker and dominate failures, so the unit of analysis matters. Bloodstream infection worries the executive but is too rare to compare locally.
